mcq: Fill in the blank: ______ is a vital arm of government which has been put in place to move the society forward.
The legislature is a vital arm of government which has been put in place to move the society forward.
Fill in the blank: ______ means the body of people who would meet to discuss the affairs of the state.
Parliament in the modern usage means the body of people who would meet to discuss the affairs of the state.
Fill in the blank: ______ is the upper law-making chamber of the British legislature.
The House of Lords is the upper law- making chamber of the British legislature.
Fill in the blank: ______ is called the Lower House, while the Senate is called the Upper House.
The House of Representatives is called the Lower House, while the Senate is called the Upper House.
Fill in the blank: ______ are called parliaments and they operate under a parliamentary system of government.
The legislatures are called parliaments and they operate under a parliamentary system of government.
fib: ______ are regarded as formal rules and procedures to guide behavior in an organisation.
Bureaucracies are regarded as formal rules and procedures to guide behavior in an organisation.
______ is an important political safeguard of the modern democratic state.
Bureaucracy is an important political safeguard of the modern democratic state.
______ is the main legislative chamber-with an elected membership of 646 persons, and the maximum life of a Parliament is five years.
The House of Commons is the main legislative chamber- with an elected membership of 646 persons, and the maximum life of a Parliament is five years.
______ is the legislative branch of the government of the United States of America.
Congress is the legislative branch of the government of the United States of America.
______ is called the House of Representative -and together with the Upper House, they form what is called the Congress.
The lower house is called the House of Representative -and together with the Upper House, they form what is called the Congress.
